corrections.summary: Added early signals for a Laravel TokenGuard authentication bypass (CVE-2026-114509), a Git recursive-clone flaw (CVE-2026-111760), a macOS authd flaw (CVE-2026-112430), a FortiOS flaw with reported public exploit code (CVE-2026-126259), a Traefik authentication bypass (CVE-2026-137481), a Budibase flaw (CVE-2026-137498) and an Android zero-click flaw (CVE-2026-58882), none yet confirmed by a vendor advisory.

items.priority_reason: Posts describe CVE-2026-114509 as an authentication bypass in a very widely deployed PHP framework; not yet confirmed with Laravel's advisory.
items.affected: Per posts: Laravel apps that use the TokenGuard api_token driver on MySQL or MariaDB. Versions not confirmed.
items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts on X and Bluesky say CVE-2026-114509 lets a request log in as an existing user without knowing their API token when a Laravel app uses the TokenGuard api_token driver with MySQL or MariaDB. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check whether your Laravel apps use the TokenGuard api_token driver on MySQL or MariaDB, and watch for Laravel's advisory and fixed release.
items.gaps: The vendor advisory was not read; affected and fixed versions come from social posts only. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: Posts say CVE-2026-111760 lets a malicious repository run code on a developer's machine during a recursive clone, and that common macOS Git builds are affected; not yet confirmed with the Git project's notice.
items.affected: Per posts: Git builds before 2.56.1, including Homebrew 2.51.0 and Apple's 2.39.5 on a tested Mac. Not confirmed with the Git project.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A post on X says CVE-2026-111760 lets a malicious repository run code on your machine when you clone it with --recurse-submodules, and that a test Mac had two vulnerable Git copies (Homebrew and Apple's). The post says the fix is in Git 2.56.1. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check which Git versions are installed on your machines (there may be more than one), avoid recursive clones of untrusted repositories, and watch for the Git project's security release notes.
items.gaps: The vendor advisory was not read; affected and fixed versions come from social posts only. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: A post says a public exploit for CVE-2026-112430 turns a failed password prompt into root on macOS; not yet confirmed with Apple's security notes.
items.affected: Per posts: macOS versions not stated.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A post on X says CVE-2026-112430 is a macOS authd flaw with public exploit code that can give a local attacker root, and urges updating. This edition has not read Apple's security notes. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check that your Macs are on the latest macOS update and look for CVE-2026-112430 in Apple's security release notes.
items.gaps: Apple's security notes were not read; the affected and fixed macOS versions are unconfirmed. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: A vulnerability-alert account reports public exploit code for CVE-2026-126259 in FortiOS, rated 9.8, with no fix listed; not yet confirmed with a Fortinet PSIRT advisory.
items.affected: Per posts: Fortinet FortiOS; versions not stated.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A post on X says public exploit code exists for CVE-2026-126259 in Fortinet FortiOS, scored 9.8, and that no fix is listed yet. This edition has not read Fortinet's PSIRT advisory. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check whether you run FortiOS devices with management interfaces reachable from the internet, and watch Fortinet's PSIRT page for an advisory on CVE-2026-126259.
items.gaps: Fortinet's PSIRT advisory was not read; affected versions and fix status are unconfirmed. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: Posts describe CVE-2026-137481 as a 9.3-rated authentication bypass in a widely used reverse proxy under specific backend setups; not yet confirmed with Traefik's advisory.
items.affected: Per posts: Traefik versions before 2.11.62, 3.7.18 and 3.8.0, when a Java or Spring backend serves both public and protected routes. Not confirmed.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A post on X says CVE-2026-137481 in Traefik can let requests get past authentication when a Java or Spring backend serves both public and protected routes, and lists fixed releases. This edition has not read Traefik's advisory. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check whether your Traefik deployments put auth middleware in front of Java or Spring backends, and watch Traefik's GitHub security advisories.
items.gaps: The vendor advisory was not read; affected and fixed versions come from social posts only. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: Posts describe CVE-2026-137498 as a 10.0-rated unauthenticated data read or delete in Budibase apps that publish MongoDB queries; not yet confirmed with Budibase's advisory.
items.affected: Per posts: Budibase before 4.0.0 with MongoDB query templates set to PUBLIC execution. Not confirmed.
items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts on X say Budibase 4.0.0 fixes nine flaws, led by CVE-2026-137498, which they say lets anyone read or delete data through a MongoDB query a builder exposed with PUBLIC execution permission. This edition has not read Budibase's advisory. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check whether your Budibase apps expose MongoDB queries with PUBLIC execution permission, and watch Budibase's GitHub security advisories.
items.gaps: The vendor advisory was not read; affected and fixed versions come from social posts only. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: A Bluesky post relays an Italian national cyber agency alert that attack code for zero-click Android flaw CVE-2026-58882 is public; not yet confirmed with Google's Android bulletin.
items.affected: Per posts: Android devices without the latest security patch; versions not stated.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A Bluesky post says Italy's national cybersecurity agency and Google urge Android users to install the latest system patches because attack code for zero-click flaw CVE-2026-58882 has been released. This edition has not read Google's Android Security Bulletin or the agency's alert. CISA KEV does not list the CVE.
items.action: Check that your Android phones show a recent security patch level, and look for CVE-2026-58882 in Google's Android Security Bulletin.
items.gaps: Google's Android Security Bulletin and the agency alert were not read; the patch level that fixes it is unconfirmed. Exploitation is unknown.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-126187 can let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code on servers using React Server Components in affected configurations; React rates it Critical (CVSS 4.0 9.5), and posts on 28 Nov say proof-of-concept code is now public.
items.affected: react-server-dom-webpack, react-server-dom-parcel and react-server-dom-turbopack 19.0.0 through 19.0.8, 19.1.0 through 19.1.9, 19.2.0 through 19.2.8, and 19.3.0. Next.js 16.0.0 through 16.4.0 apps using the App Router with Cache Components and a `use cache` function that returns multiple typed arrays (Next.js advisory GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr).
items.summary: A deserialization flaw in React Server Components (CVE-2026-126187) can lead to remote code execution from crafted payloads when a response carries multiple typed arrays and an attacker-controlled value. React says only rare cases are affected but recommends updating immediately; apps that don't use a server or an RSC-capable framework are not affected. Next.js published a matching advisory for `use cache` functions that return multiple typed arrays and says there is no workaround. The advisories date from October and November; posts on X on 28 Nov say proof-of-concept code and a test lab are now public, which we have not verified. No exploitation has been confirmed and it is not in CISA KEV.
items.action: Upgrade the react-server-dom packages to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 or later in your line, and Next.js 16 apps to 16.4.1 or later (16.4.6 is the current release).
steps: Check whether your app uses React Server Components through a framework or bundler plugin (react-server-dom-webpack, -parcel or -turbopack).
Upgrade those packages to 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1 or later, matching your release line.
For Next.js 16.0.0 through 16.4.0, upgrade to 16.4.1 or later even if you don't have a `use cache` function returning typed arrays; Next.js lists no workaround.
items.gaps: Public proof-of-concept is reported only by social posts and was not checked. Next.js releases after 16.4.1 were not reviewed for further security fixes. The Next.js advisory carries no CVE id; it is linked to CVE-2026-126187 by posts and its matching description, not by the advisory itself. FIRST EPSS dated 2026-11-27. CISA KEV catalogVersion 2026.11.27 checked.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-129289 can let an unauthenticated attacker run PHP code through PHP-FPM when the web server reuses FastCGI connections; PHP rates it Critical (CVSS 4.0 9.2), a detailed research write-up was published on 28 Nov, and its EPSS is 0.44.
items.affected: PHP before 8.2.36, 8.3.0 before 8.3.37, 8.4.0 before 8.4.28, and 8.5.0 before 8.5.13, when running under PHP-FPM (or LSAPI) with persistent backend connections (FCGI_KEEP_CONN).
items.summary: PHP can fail to discard unread request-body bytes before reusing a persistent PHP-FPM or LSAPI connection (CVE-2026-129289). When an app opens php://input without reading it to the end, an unauthenticated attacker can make the leftover bytes form a separate FastCGI request, bypass front-end routing and run attacker-controlled PHP code with the worker's privileges. It requires connection reuse between the web server and PHP-FPM. PHP fixed it on 19 Nov; a researcher's detailed write-up circulated on 28 Nov. No exploitation has been confirmed and it is not in CISA KEV.
items.action: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 or later and restart PHP-FPM.
steps: Upgrade PHP to 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28 or 8.5.13 or later in your release line (or your distribution's patched package), then restart PHP-FPM.
Check whether your web server reuses FastCGI connections to PHP-FPM (for example nginx `fastcgi_keep_conn on`); those setups are the ones exposed.
items.gaps: The interim workaround of turning off FastCGI connection reuse comes from search summaries, not from the PHP advisory text we read, so it is left out of the steps. Later PHP releases were not reviewed for further security fixes. FIRST EPSS dated 2026-11-27. CISA KEV catalogVersion 2026.11.27 checked.
